Hi Sarah / Rahul — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track action items. Attachment: redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.pdf

Summary of needs we heard
- High-throughput Q&A for internal knowledge base (low single-digit-second latencies for SLOs).
- Multi-region routing (US primary, EU fallback) to meet compliance and latency objectives.
- Cost-conscious routing policies: route bulk/low-priority requests to quantized cheaper variants; reserve low-latency variants for interactive UI.
- Embedding-based semantic search + reranker for top-k results (embedding store you host or via our managed index).
- Auth: SSO + per-route API keys for third-party integrations, and key rotation policy.

Immediate next steps
1) Tech dive with your engineering team to validate SDK auth flow & network egress (please loop in your infra lead).
2) We’ll share a starter routing/policy template and SDK init snippet.
3) Proposed timeline: tech dive this week, then a 2-week pilot with a single route (UI interactive) to validate latency & fallbacks.

Ask: can you confirm the best tech contact and a couple of 1-hour slots on Thursday or Friday PST?

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & model routing requirements — architecture notes

Hey Jason / team — quick architecture/implementation notes to prep for the tech dive. Sharing two small artifact examples attached: routing-config-sample.yaml and example-fallback-policy.json

1) SDK setup & auth (example)
- Python init snippet:

  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", region="us-west-2", timeout=10)

  # Per-route override example
  client.create_route(name="ui-interactive", model_variant="redwood-gpt-2.7b-lowlatency", max_tokens=512, timeout=5)

Notes: we recommend per-route API keys if you need to scope access for downstream tools; SSO + SCIM for team provisioning is available for Dedicated/Private.

2) Model routing & policy config (high level)
- Latency tiers:
  - low_latency: p99 <= 1.5s, model_variant: redwood-gpt-2.7b-lowlatency (higher cost)
  - standard: p99 <= 3s, model_variant: redwood-gpt-2.7b-standard
  - cost_optimized: batchable / quantized variants for non-interactive tasks

- Fallback chains: route->if_capacity_full->fallback_variant->if_region_unavailable->regional-fallback
  Example policy (see attachment) includes rules for: capacity thresholds, cost budget per 10k tokens, and region routing preferences (us-west primary, eu-west fallback).

3) Structured output / tool calling
- For your RAG use cases recommend structured tool-calling for actions (e.g., ticket create, KB augment) and a strict JSON schema for outputs that the client validates.

4) Embeddings & reranker recommendations
- Option A (managed): Redwood-hosted index with hybrid approximate NN (fast, simpler auth).
- Option B (self-hosted): you host embeddings in your vector DB; we provide signed URLs + ephemeral tokens for query.
- Reranker: use a small reranker model placed after semantic-retrieval to improve precision on short lists (1-5).

Next steps from our side
- I’ll bring a starter routing-config and fallback-policy to the tech dive.
- Dev will prepare embedding options and an example reranker config.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & model routing requirements — embedding & reranker notes

Quick notes from the embeddings/reranker perspective:
- If you self-host embeddings, the SDK supports async signed-query tokens to avoid long-lived credentials.
- For semantic search at scale, shard your index by product vertical to reduce recall latency and make reranker input smaller.
- Reranker placement: run after retrieving top-20, then score top-5 for final UI. Use a 350M-1B parameter reranker to balance cost vs quality.
- Instrumentation: enable token-level cost logging and per-route tracing (we provide a tracing header X-Redwood-Trace-Id you can propagate).

If you can share expected qps and vector size, I’ll produce a recommended batch size and quantization profile for the pilot.

— Dev
